title: Pea and Mint Soup
subtitle: Bright blended soup of frozen peas and fresh mint
excerpt: Frozen peas simmered briefly in vegetable stock and blended with fresh mint and a little cream. Brilliant green and ready in under 20 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pea and mint soup became popular in British home cooking in the 1990s and 2000s as the frozen pea came to be recognised as a genuinely good ingredient rather than a second-rate substitute for fresh. Frozen peas are picked and frozen within hours of harvest, making them sweeter and more consistent than most fresh peas available in supermarkets. Mint has been paired with peas in British cooking since the 18th century at least, as both grow well together and the herb cuts the sweetness of the legume. The soup needs almost no cooking: the peas are added to hot stock and barely simmered to preserve their colour and freshness.

recipeTools.notes: And a stick blender or jug blender.

content.text: Do not overcook the peas: prolonged boiling destroys the vivid green colour and the fresh flavour. Simmer for no more than 3 to 4 minutes from frozen, then blend immediately. Plunging the blended soup into a bowl of iced water after blending will preserve the colour if it is not being served immediately.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic. Cook for 1 minute. Pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Add the frozen peas. Return to a simmer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes only.
Remove from heat. Add the mint leaves and cream. Blend immediately until completely smooth. Season and serve at once. Garnish with a swirl of cream and a few fresh mint leaves if you like.
